newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NORTHAM MINERS CONTINUE STRIKE OVER WAGES.
newsitem.headline: NORTHAM MINERS CONTINUE STRIKE OVER WAGES.

text.p: A strike by about 5,000 mineworkers at Northam Platinum Ltd is continuing, mine managers Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said on Monday.
"The strike at Northam is continuing. Management is at this very moment in talks with the union," a Gold Fields spokesman told Reuters.
The strike over 1996/7 wages increases began last Thursday night when the night shift did not go underground.
Gold Fields said it was "too early at this stage" to estimate how much production had been lost to the strike.
"Management is doing everything in its power to bring production back to normal. The strike has taken place over the weekend," the spokesman said.
Gold Fields said in a statement last Friday that if the strike was of "short duration" production should continue at "planned levels" before the strike.
The majority of Northam's National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) members voted in favour of striking after management and the union deadlocked over wages on September 26.
The union had initially demanded a 15 percent pay hike but was prepared to accept management's offer of 10 percent.
The dispute arose out of the union's demand for additional quarterly increases aimed at reaching parity with wages paid on gold mines of the Gold Fields group.
Northam produced 75,365 ounces of precious metals in concentrates in the three months to September.
The mine recorded a net loss before capital spending of 7.39 million rand in the September quarter after turning in a profit of 8.17 million in the previous quarter.
